I'm noting the environment has 4 RTX 3090 GPUs, MPI, OpenMP, and nvcc 12.0, so I need to preserve the exact output semantics — the benchmark name, size, validation, timing, GFLOPS, and result printing must all stay identical, meaning the computed matrix C has to match bit-for-bit for the hash to validate.\n\nI'm realizing the serial k-reduction sum in double isn't auto-vectorized without -ffast-math, so it runs strictly sequential, and with gnu++20 (extensions on) plus -march=native, GCC defaults to -ffp-contract=fast, meaning it silently fuses multiply-adds into FMA instructions. Since nvcc also contracts FMA by default, I can match this behavior on the GPU by using FMA accumulation in the same sequential order across k, which should let me preserve bitwise identical results between CPU and GPU implementations.\n\nTo be safe, I'll use explicit `std::fma` on both CPU and GPU (CUDA's `fma()` is IEEE-correct) to guarantee deterministic, identical results, and then verify this by building the original binary and comparing full-matrix hash output bitwise using the `-r` option. For parallelization, my plan is to distribute A across MPI ranks using row-block partitioning, giving each rank roughly N/P rows.\n\nEach rank broadcasts the full B matrix, computes its own row block of C, and gathers results back to rank 0 for printing and validation. Within each rank, I'll assign a GPU (chosen via node-local rank through MPI_Comm_split_type SHARED) to handle most of the row computation, while OpenMP parallelizes initialization, host-side packing, and any CPU-side share of rows, balancing work based on the GPU's much higher FP32/FP64 throughput compared to the CPU's many cores — though the strict-order summation limits vectorization opportunities over k, it still allows parallelizing over j.\n\nI'm thinking through whether CPU could actually rival or beat the GPU on FP64 given the weak FP64 rate on consumer GPUs versus the raw core count of a 256-core CPU, but since CUDA must be used unconditionally, I'll split each rank's local rows between GPU and CPU threads by some ratio, relying on the fact that results stay bitwise identical as long as every chunk uses the same sequential, FMA-consistent per-element arithmetic regardless of which device computes it.\n\nI'm deciding to determine the GPU/CPU split fraction empirically by benchmarking each kernel separately rather than hardcoding a guess, and to settle how timing should be measured -- deciding that the computation timer should span from before the multiply through the final gather to rank 0, including device transfers, since all of that work is necessary to produce a valid result on rank 0.\n\nFor data setup, I'm planning to have each rank compute only its own local rows of A directly rather than broadcasting, since B is fully deterministic and cheap to generate locally on every rank, and I'll parallelize initialization with OpenMP. For validation, since rank 0 needs access to a few early rows of A and the full B matrix, I'm checking that rank 0 always owns row 0 so the row-block distribution scheme still satisfies the validation requirements without forcing every rank to materialize the entire A matrix, which would hurt memory scalability for large N.\n\nSince A's values come from a pure function of indices, I realize validation can just call that function directly rather than needing the distributed rows at all. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793087536387,"sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01KF24a73bkZ7t5tqWGhLLHh","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA matrix multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   MPI     Rows of A and C are block-distributed across ranks. Every rank\n//           generates its own rows of A and the full B (the generator is a\n//           pure function), so no input communication is required.\n//   CUDA    Each rank drives one GPU (local rank modulo device count).\n//   OpenMP  One team thread drives the GPU; the remaining threads compute on\n//           the CPU with a register-blocked, packed-B kernel.\n//           Both devices claim 64x64 output tiles from a shared atomic counter,\n//           so the faster device automatically receives more tiles.\n//\n// Numerical semantics: every element C[i][j] is accumulated as\n//   acc = fma(A[i][k], B[k][j], acc)   for k = 0 .. N-1 in ascending order,\n// on both CPU and GPU, so the result is bitwise independent of the decomposition\n// and identical to the original serial triple loop (built with FMA contraction).\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <atomic>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr size_t TILE = 64;        // output tile edge (rows and columns)\nconstexpr size_t MR = 4;           // CPU micro-kernel rows\nconstexpr size_t NR = 8;           // CPU micro-kernel columns (packed B panel width)\nconstexpr size_t GPU_BATCH = 16;   // tiles claimed per GPU launch\nconstexpr size_t GPU_BK = 16;      // GPU k-step (shared-memory tile depth)\nconstexpr int GPU_THREADS = 256;   // 16x16 threads, each computing a 4x4 sub-tile\n\n#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,     \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\n// Fill nRows rows (starting at global row firstRow) of an N-column matrix.\nvoid initRows(double* mat, const size_t firstRow, const size_t nRows, const size_t N) {\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < nRows; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, firstRow + i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Pack B into column panels of width NR: Bp[(p*N + k)*NR + c] = B[k][p*NR + c] (zero padded).\nvoid packB(const double* B, double* Bp, const size_t N) {\n    const size_t npan = (N + NR - 1) / NR;\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t p = 0; p < npan; ++p) {\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n            for (size_t c = 0; c < NR; ++c) {\n                const size_t col = p * NR + c;\n                Bp[(p * N + k) * NR + c] = (col < N) ? B[k * N + col] : 0.0;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Shared, read-only state for one rank plus the dynamic tile counter.\nstruct RankContext {\n    size_t N;           // matrix dimension\n    size_t rowsLocal;   // rows of A/C owned by this rank\n    size_t rowsPad;     // rowsLocal rounded up to TILE (zero padded A rows)\n    size_t CG;          // tile columns: ceil(N / TILE)\n    size_t NPAN;        // packed B panels: ceil(N / NR)\n    size_t numTiles;    // ceil(rowsLocal / TILE) * CG\n    const double* A;    // rowsPad x N, row-major\n    const double* B;    // N x N, row-major\n    const double* Bp;   // packed B\n    double* C;          // rowsLocal x N, row-major (pinned, mapped for GPU writes)\n    std::atomic<size_t> nextTile{0};\n};\n\n// CPU micro-kernel: acc[MR][NR] += A(MR rows) * Bpanel over k = 0..N-1 in order.\ninline void microKernel(const double* a, const double* bp, const size_t N,\n                        double (&acc)[MR][NR]) noexcept {\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n        const double* b = bp + k * NR;\n        for (size_t r = 0; r < MR; ++r) {\n            const double av = a[r * N + k];\n            for (size_t c = 0; c < NR; ++c) {\n                acc[r][c] = std::fma(av, b[c], acc[r][c]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid cpuTile(const RankContext& ctx, const size_t t) noexcept {\n    const size_t N = ctx.N;\n    const size_t rowBase = (t / ctx.CG) * TILE;\n    const size_t pBegin = (t % ctx.CG) * (TILE / NR);\n    const size_t pEnd = std::min(pBegin + TILE / NR, ctx.NPAN);\n\n    for (size_t mt = 0; mt < TILE; mt += MR) {\n        const size_t r0 = rowBase + mt;\n        if (r0 >= ctx.rowsLocal) break;\n        const size_t rows = std::min(MR, ctx.rowsLocal - r0);\n\n        for (size_t p = pBegin; p < pEnd; ++p) {\n            double acc[MR][NR] = {};\n            microKernel(ctx.A + r0 * N, ctx.Bp + p * N * NR, N, acc);\n\n            const size_t cols = std::min(NR, N - p * NR);\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {\n                for (size_t c = 0; c < cols; ++c) {\n                    ctx.C[(r0 + r) * N + p * NR + c] = acc[r][c];\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// GPU kernel: one block per 64x64 output tile, 16x16 threads, each thread owns a 4x4\n// sub-tile. The k loop advances in BK-deep shared-memory tiles in ascending order, so each\n// accumulator sees the exact same sequence of fma operations as the CPU kernel.\n__global__ void gemmTilesKernel(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n                                double* __restrict__ C, const size_t firstTile,\n                                const size_t CG, const size_t rowsLocal, const size_t N) {\n    __shared__ double As[GPU_BK][TILE];   // As[kk][row]\n    __shared__ double Bs[GPU_BK][TILE];   // Bs[kk][col]\n\n    const size_t t = firstTile + blockIdx.x;\n    const size_t rowBase = (t / CG) * TILE;\n    const size_t colBase = (t % CG) * TILE;\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int tx = tid % 16;\n    const int ty = tid / 16;\n\n    double acc[4][4] = {};\n\n    for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += GPU_BK) {\n        const int kLen = (int)((N - k0 < GPU_BK) ? (N - k0) : GPU_BK);\n\n        // Load A tile (64 x 16) and B tile (16 x 64): 1024 elements each, 4 per thread.\n        #pragma unroll\n        for (int m = 0; m < 4; ++m) {\n            const int idx = tid + m * GPU_THREADS;\n            const int r = idx / (int)GPU_BK;\n            const int kk = idx % (int)GPU_BK;\n            double av = 0.0;\n            if (kk < kLen && rowBase + r < rowsLocal) {\n                av = A[(rowBase + r) * N + k0 + kk];\n            }\n            As[kk][r] = av;\n\n            const int kb = idx / (int)TILE;\n            const int c = idx % (int)TILE;\n            double bv = 0.0;\n            if (kb < kLen && colBase + c < N) {\n                bv = B[(k0 + kb) * N + colBase + c];\n            }\n            Bs[kb][c] = bv;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < kLen; ++kk) {\n            double a[4], b[4];\n            #pragma unroll\n            for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {\n                a[i] = As[kk][ty + 16 * i];   // interleaved for conflict-free shared reads\n                b[i] = Bs[kk][tx + 16 * i];\n            }\n            #pragma unroll\n            for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {\n                #pragma unroll\n                for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) {\n                    acc[i][j] = fma(a[i], b[j], acc[i][j]);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    #pragma unroll\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {\n        #pragma unroll\n        for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) {\n            const size_t row = rowBase + ty + 16 * i;\n            const size_t col = colBase + tx + 16 * j;\n            if (row < rowsLocal && col < N) {\n                C[row * N + col] = acc[i][j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Runs on OpenMP thread 0: drives this rank's GPU, claiming batches of tiles.\nvoid gpuWorker(RankContext& ctx, const int device) {\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaSetDevice(device));\n    if (ctx.numTiles == 0) return;\n\n    const size_t N = ctx.N;\n    double* dA = nullptr;\n    double* dB = nullptr;\n    double* dC = nullptr;\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, ctx.rowsPad * N * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, N * N * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaHostGetDevicePointer(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&dC), ctx.C, 0));\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, ctx.A, ctx.rowsPad * N * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, ctx.B, N * N * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    for (;;) {\n        const size_t t0 = ctx.nextTile.fetch_add(GPU_BATCH);\n        if (t0 >= ctx.numTiles) break;\n        const size_t count = std::min(GPU_BATCH, ctx.numTiles - t0);\n\n        gemmTilesKernel<<<static_cast<unsigned int>(count), GPU_THREADS>>>(\n            dA, dB, dC, t0, ctx.CG, ctx.rowsLocal, N);\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());\n        CHECK_CUDA(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    }\n\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));\n}\n\n// Runs on the remaining OpenMP threads: claims tiles and computes them on the CPU.\nvoid cpuWorker(RankContext& ctx) {\n    for (;;) {\n        const size_t t = ctx.nextTile.fetch_add(1);\n        if (t >= ctx.numTiles) break;\n        cpuTile(ctx, t);\n    }\n}\n\n// Validation on rank 0. `actual` holds the 5x5 sampled C entries (row-major over pi, pj).\nbool validateResult(const double* B, const double* actual, const size_t N) {\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n\n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n\n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += getPseudoRndValue(N, i, k) * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n\n            const double actualVal = actual[pi * 5 + pj];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actualVal - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n\n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actualVal, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int nranks = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &nranks);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line N;\n    ctx.rowsLocal = rowsLocal;\n    ctx.CG = (N + TILE - 1) / TILE;\n    ctx.rowsPad = ((rowsLocal + TILE - 1) / TILE) * TILE;\n    ctx.NPAN = (N + NR - 1) / NR;\n    ctx.numTiles = (ctx.rowsPad / CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&A),\n                              std::max<size_t>(1, ctx.rowsPad * N) * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMallocHost(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&B), std::max<size_t>(1, N * N) * sizeof(double)));\n    CHECK_CUDA(cudaHostAlloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&C),\n                             std::max<size_t>(1, rowsLocal * N) * sizeof(double), cudaHostAllocMapped));\n    std::vector<double> Bp(ctx.NPAN * N * NR);\n\n    if (root) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initRows(A, rowStart, rowsLocal, N);\n    if (ctx.rowsPad > rowsLocal) {\n        std::memset(A + rowsLocal * N, 0, (ctx.rowsPad - rowsLocal) * N * sizeof(double));\n    }\n    initRows(B, 0, N, N);\n    packB(B, Bp.data(), N);\n\n    ctx.A = A;\n    ctx.B = B;\n    ctx.Bp = Bp.data();\n    ctx.C = C;\n\n    // Perform matrix multiplication\n    if (root) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        if (omp_get_thread_num() == 0) {\n            gpuWorker(ctx, device);\n        } else {\n            cpuWorker(ctx);\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / std::vector<double> fullC;\n        std::vector<int> counts;\n        std::vector<int> displs;\n        if (root) {\n            fullC.resize(N * N);\n            counts.resize(nranks);\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793087716935,"sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","part":{"id":"prt_17c5af146001t7C7oLNI555hTv","messageID":"msg_17c5aed7a001dnBRdTYCGjj6qu","sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","type":"reasoning","text":"Looking at the numbers, GPU-only gets about 110 GF at 4096, lower than I'd expect. Adding CPU threads roughly doubles throughput to 225 GF for a single rank, and scaling to four ranks with four GPUs pushes it up to around 539 GF.\n\nThere's some timing noise with 1000-size problems (10ms vs 93ms earlier), likely from CUDA context setup, nothing concerning. Given limited effort budget, I'm weighing two improvement paths: tweaking GPU tile sizes or buffering strategy for maybe a 1.5-2x gain, versus looking at why the CPU microkernel is only hitting ~0.5 GF per core when AVX2 peak should be much higher — that's the more suspicious gap worth digging into first.\n\nI suspect the compiler isn't vectorizing the accumulator loop properly, possibly falling back to scalar FMA, but even scalar peak would be ~12 GF per core, so 0.5 GF is 25x below even that floor — something more fundamental is wrong, likely memory bandwidth since each microkernel streams hundreds of KB of A and B panel data per call.\n\nThis confirms the bottleneck is arithmetic intensity: roughly 3 bytes streamed per FMA is far too low, meaning we're DRAM/L3-bound rather than compute-bound at N=4096. The fix requires proper cache blocking — keeping a B panel resident in L2 while reusing it across many row-microtiles so A rows are read while B stays hot, rather than re-streaming both from memory on every microkernel call.\n\nI'm planning to use the C memory itself as the running accumulator across kc chunks, since it's pinned host memory the CPU can write into directly for its own tile — but I need to make sure the very first chunk initializes correctly rather than accumulating onto stale data.\n\nI'm also considering a simpler alternative: keeping a per-tile local accumulator array on the stack, sized to fit in L1/L2, and only writing out to C for valid rows/columns while skipping padded entries.\n\nWriting tiling loop code...\n\nThis fits within L2 fine. The zero-padding for partial rows and columns keeps the computation correct without special-casing, and the microKernel's stride-N access pattern across four rows gives sequential reads within each row, so prefetching should work well. I'm now turning to thinking about how to improve the GPU kernel.\n\nI should also check thread counts per rank on CPU, then move to implementing k-blocking with KC=256. Writing the cpuTile function...\n\nStill writing microkernel loop...\n\nFinishing the microKernel loop body, then checking the Bp panel layout indexing matches the stride and offsets expected, with N passed as stride. I'll need to edit the file to add this along with the cpuTile signature and the KC=256 constant.\n\n","time":{"start":1793087697222,"end":1793087716895},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793087716936,"sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","part":{"id":"prt_17c5b3e24001SjnE1TTArEF7yf","messageID":"msg_17c5aed7a001dnBRdTYCGjj6qu","sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","type":"text","text":"Scaling is reasonable (4 GPUs reach about 540-630 GFLOPS), but the CPU contribution is far below what 255 AVX2 cores should deliver: roughly 0.5 GFLOPS per core. The cause is the kernel's memory traffic. Each 4x8 microtile streams its entire A rows and B panel, about 3 bytes per FMA, so it is bandwidth-bound. I'll add k-blocking (KC=256) with the per-tile accumulators kept in a local buffer. Each element still accumulates k in ascending order, so results stay bitwise identical.","time":{"start":1793087716900,"end":1793087716917}}}

But estimating total DRAM/L3 traffic for B panels across all tiles gives roughly 8GB for N=4096, which at the observed runtime implies only ~16 GB/s of bandwidth usage — well under the ~300 GB/s available on a 2-socket EPYC, so bandwidth alone doesn't explain the slowdown and I need to dig into what else could be bottlenecking throughput.\n\nFor N=2048 the numbers work out to about 11 GB/s, still far from peak, pointing toward something like L2/L3 miss rates or reuse inefficiency rather than raw bandwidth. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793087897625,"sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","part":{"id":"prt_17c5dcaa700177IBE5Zn7RLmeu","messageID":"msg_17c5dc365001zmCUbamViV0Ken","sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","type":"reasoning","text":"Single-thread performance comes in at 1.15 GF, far below the peak of 24-48 GF, and scales linearly with thread count — so this points to per-core compute inefficiency rather than contention between threads. I'm noting that 1.15 GF per thread works out to roughly 0.4 flops/cycle, which seems low for what should be achievable.\n\nI'm checking the kernel's FMA throughput — theoretical peak should be 16 flops/cycle with 4-wide FMA on doubles, so running at 1/16th of that is a big gap. I trace through the loop: 8 vfmadd ops per k-iteration across 2 ymm registers per row with MR=4, giving 64 flops per k, and I check whether the A matrix access pattern (strided by lda) is causing cache line issues — though sequential k access seems fine since 8 k-iterations fit per cache line. I also consider whether register spilling is happening given a memory operand showing up, but with only 8 ymm accumulators plus broadcasts, register pressure shouldn't be the bottleneck — though I wonder if accumulators aren't actually staying in registers through the whole kernel. I briefly consider whether nvcc's handling of `-march=native` compiler flags could be stripping out the vectorization, but confirm the vfmadd instructions are indeed present in the assembly.\n\nRunning the numbers again: each accumulator chain has a 4-5 cycle FMA latency on Zen3, but with 8 independent chains running in parallel I should get full 2-FMA-per-cycle throughput, landing around 4 cycles per k-iteration and roughly 48 GFLOPS at 3GHz — yet I'm measuring just 1.15 GFLOPS, a 20x shortfall implying each k-iteration is taking ~80 cycles instead of 4. I rule out cache misses since both the B panel and buf copy-in/out seem to have fully sequential access patterns with negligible overhead. This leaves me suspecting the compiler isn't keeping accumulators in registers across iterations — maybe reloading them from memory each time because they're passed by reference into an inlined function.\n\nThe assembly confirms it: FMA instructions are operating directly on a stack memory address rather than a register, meaning the accumulator array lives in memory and each update suffers store-to-load forwarding latency through a dependency chain — which lines up with the ~20x slowdown I'm seeing. My fix is to restructure the microkernel so the accumulator array is a genuinely local variable, likely by passing it in and returning it by value as a small struct rather than by reference, since that should make scalar replacement of aggregates more likely to succeed and keep everything in registers. I'm sketching out a struct-based version of the microkernel that copies the accumulator in, runs the k-loop, and returns the updated accumulator by value, planning to test this change on a scratch copy first and check the generated assembly to confirm the stack spill disappears.\n\n","time":{"start":1793087883943,"end":1793087897563},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

The accumulator is a local register block;\n// k is visited in ascending order, so accumulation order matches the serial reference.\ninline void microKernel(const double* __restrict a, const size_t lda,\n                        const double* __restrict bp, const size_t kLen,\n                        double* __restrict c) noexcept {\n    double acc[MR][NR];\n    for (size_t r = 0; r < MR; ++r) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < NR; ++j) {\n            acc[r][j] = c[r * TILE + j];\n        }\n    }\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < kLen; ++k) {\n        const double* b = bp + k * NR;\n        for (size_t r = 0; {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793090009620,"sessionID":"ses_e83acd711ffeAGzMG6P0UDE4Dw","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"read","callID":"toolu_01XL6bo8wGGupcGja9acu5Mq","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp","limit":260},"output":"<path>/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/matmul/matmul.cpp</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: // Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA matrix multiplication benchmark.\n2: //\n3: // Decomposition:\n4: //   MPI     Rows of A and C are block-distributed across ranks.
